item.text: I’m inspecting the current implementation again to find a refactor that changes structure in a useful way, not just style. On a codebase this small, the bar is removing a real maintenance smell.

I found the next useful split: the current checker still mixes two concerns, bracket classification and stack-based validation. I’m separating those so the validator only handles nesting, while a dedicated bracket profile defines which characters are treated as delimiters.
The implementation is split cleanly now. I’m making a small follow-up in the tests so the non-`String` path is exercised with another `CharSequence` implementation, then I’ll run the suite.
I’m compiling and running the refactored code now, plus one CLI sanity check after the API simplification.

item.text:
Refactored [BalancedParentheses.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BalancedParentheses.java:1) to separate bracket definition from validation. The public API is now just `isBalanced(CharSequence)`, which delegates to a `BalanceChecker` for stack logic and a `BracketProfile` for delimiter rules. That removes the previous mixed responsibility where one type handled both parsing and matching behavior.

I also extended [BalancedParenthesesTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BalancedParenthesesTest.java:1) to exercise the `CharSequence` API with both `StringBuilder` and `CharBuffer`, while keeping the existing parameterized cases and null-input contract.

Verified with:
```sh
mkdir -p build/test-classes && javac -cp lib/junit-platform-console-standalone-1.10.2.jar -d build/test-classes BalancedParentheses.java BalancedParenthesesTest.java && java -jar lib/junit-platform-console-standalone-1.10.2.jar execute --class-path build/test-classes --scan-class-path
```
All 10 tests passed. I also sanity-checked `main` with `java -cp build/test-classes BalancedParentheses "{[()]}"`, which returned `true`.
